heuristics.statement: Four parts. (a) The chaining value cv = F_38(IV, M0) of a random first block is an independent random value for the claw maps F(a0) and P(u) and for the later events, so the windows of the program are independent trials. (b) The yield and the cost of a window are those measured on the real step function over the 24 pre-declared windows of 2^25 walk evaluations: 36,397.58 distinct claws, 36,278.38 distinct claw groups and 17,504.1 operations per distinct claw on average (the most conservative of the pooled one-sided 99.9% Student-t bounds and each 8-window run set's own one-sided 99% bounds: mu+ = 645,297,157 operations per window, c- = 36,127.96 claws, g- = 35,770.49 groups, r- = 0.996276 groups per claw); the program cannot be run for 2^71.4508 windows. (c) A distinct claw group (claws sharing a0 or u form one group; one is counted) is a trial of the accepted event with probability p_claw = q_pf x q3r = 2^-87.593798 (H1-P1 with the charged q_pf = 2^-16.192770, H2-P1), independent of the walk's yield. (d) The a0 of a claw is uniform in the window R = 9 and its a1 = u - h(a0, cv) is uniform over the attack, so the exact post-filter counts of H1-P1 apply to C1, C2 and F7; G is charged at the lower bound measured on this program's claws.
heuristics.scope: The fixed target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 and the program experiments/r38joint.py: first blocks drawn uniformly, windows of 2^25 walk evaluations of the real maps F and P with the class-P parameters, claws defined by the exact offset test of proof.md Lemma 2 with the window's four heads. Not claimed for another characteristic, another round count or another walk.
heuristics.extrapolation: Part (b) is measured over 24 pre-declared full windows (proof.md Section 5 and Appendix A; per-window operations per distinct claw within [17,070.8, 17,916.0]) and extended to 2^71.4508 windows by (a). Part (d): a0 = (9 << 26) | 26 bits of the predecessor point, u = 28 point bits with a 4-bit mix; measured post-filter rates over 1,127,181 raw claws: C1 0.1248 (exact 1/8), C2 | C1 0.0995 (exact 0.0989), G | C1 C2 charged at 0.0161433 (distinct-claw rate 0.017773, raw 0.01801; exact 0.0162004); the organizer sandbox asserts every claw of four windows of 2^20 evaluations against the real E16x and the real words W7, W8, W9 of both members (r38-window-small).
heuristics.limitations: The organizer sandbox runs windows of 2^20 evaluations (about 180 distinct claws per window), the offline measurement 24 windows of 2^25 (873,542 distinct claws); the extrapolation from 24 windows to 2^71.4508 windows is part (a). Within one chaining value only 2^28 of the 2^32 values of u are reachable (part (d) is about the attack-wide law).

heuristics.statement: Transfer premise, inherited from newjordan 51613d1c (its H1-P1, proof Section 6): the probability that a claw passes the four post-filters C1 (W8y - W8x = D8), C2 (s0(W9y) - s0(W9x) = D9s), G (s0(W8y) - s0(W8x) = T8) and F7 (W7y - W7x = D7 and s0(W7y) - s0(W7x) = F7d) is q_pf = 57,726,359,870,197 x 287,309,824 / 2^90 = 2^-16.1877, the exact count over a0 uniform in the window R = 9 and a1 uniform over 2^32 (C1, C2 read only a1; G reads (a0, a1); F7 reads (a0, a1, cv) and its count 287,309,824 / 2^32 is cv-averaged), and it is the rate for the claws this program finds, except that the G stage is charged at the lower of two one-sided 99% Wilson lower bounds when below the exact rate: on DISTINCT claws (G 575 of 32,352 distinct C2 passes = 0.017773, bound 0.0161433) and on raw counts with the rediscovery-corrected n_eff (G 755 of 41,929 raw C2 passes = 0.01801, bound 0.0163690); charged 0.0161433, q_pf = 2^-16.192770 (proof.md Section 5).
heuristics.scope: The claws of experiments/r38joint.py: a0 in R = 9 by construction, a1 = u - h(a0, cv) with u in the 2^28-element per-cv set of proof.md Section 3; the four filters are computed by the program on the real words (asserted against variantW in check mode).
heuristics.extrapolation: The exact counts are 51613d1c's (own exhaustive enumerations, accepted on this board); this program re-measures the stage rates on its claws (proof.md Section 5: C1 0.1248, C2 | C1 0.0995 over the 24 evaluation windows; G | C1 C2 0.01801 pooled over 24 + 48 windows, 755 of 41,929) and charges G at its measured lower bound where that is below the exact value.
heuristics.limitations: The counts were not re-enumerated here (2^32 and 2^58 enumerations in C by 51613d1c); F7 and step 3b are rare at the measured scale (11 F7 passes over 24 windows), so their rates are inherited, not measured.

heuristics.statement: Transfer premise, inherited from 51613d1c (its H2-P1 and H10, proof Section 9): a good pair (a claw passing C1 C2 G F7) is accepted by step 3b (the two second blocks collide) with probability q3r >= q3_P1 x 2^32 / 160 = 2^-71.4010, q3_P1 = 2^-96.0791 = q3_model x 2^D_LB with q3_model = 2^-96.0133 (the A0-variant family's registered accepted-event rate: 128 seeds x 2^28 samples for the level, 400 seeds for the relaxation ratio, two one-sided 99% bounds, union 98%) and D_LB = -0.0658 (the one-sided 99% lower bound of the paired P1-minus-A0 difference on window R = 9 over 36 seeds; point estimate -0.0121). New in this program and declared here: a window's claws have their row-16 pass among 4 heads x 8 offsets (one of five 4-head subsets, cycled from a uniform random start in the attack and from a seed-derived start in the measured windows, whose per-subset yields are reported and whose smallest bound is charged) instead of all 160; the attack-wide mixture over the 160 passes is uniform given equal per-subset claw yields (measured: the five subset means of distinct groups per window agree within 0.2%, proof.md Section 5), which is the mixture 51613d1c's measurement pools over, and the acceptance rate conditional on a 4-head subset is taken to average to q3r over the five subsets as used.
heuristics.scope: Good pairs of this program on window R = 9 with the five head subsets rotated per window; the accepted event is the exact equality of the eight second-block output words (proof.md Lemma 1), a superset of 51613d1c's cell-tested step 3b, so its rate is at least 51613d1c's.
heuristics.extrapolation: Not re-measured: the deep rows fire at ~2^-71 per good pair and the leader's measurement tool (a C program, 36 seeds x 2^28 samples per seed) is outside the organizer sandbox and this submission. The only head/window dependence within reach was measured by 51613d1c A.26 at the r16 | all4 gate (298 events; -0.116 +/- 0.167 between windows, consistent with zero); its deeper transfer was declared there (H10) and accepted; this submission declares the analogous transfer for the head subsets.
heuristics.limitations: If the acceptance rate of good pairs differed between 4-head subsets, the attack-wide rate would still be the uniform mixture (the subsets rotate), but the per-window variance of accepted pairs would grow; the claim uses only the mixture. A materially lower deep rate than 51613d1c's registered bound would raise time_log2 one for one in log2 q3r; the registered margin is 0.0537 bit (D_LB against its point estimate) plus the 98% union of the base.

heuristics.statement: Claws of one window that share no endpoint are independent trials of the accepted event (51613d1c H3-P1, measured there on 24 chaining values and on the forced-bit events of rows 17..21 within one chaining value); the program counts one claw per endpoint-sharing group (r- = 0.996276 groups per claw).
heuristics.scope: Distinct claws of one window of this program (36,397.58 per window, against 2^33 per chaining value in 51613d1c, so the within-window dependence is far smaller than the one 51613d1c bounded).
heuristics.extrapolation: Groups are counted exactly per window (count_groups); the premise is the independence of the deep event between groups, inherited.
heuristics.limitations: Independence of the rows 17..37 event between distinct groups of one chaining value is not testable at any sample size (as 51613d1c states).

heuristics.statement: A_C = 2^78, A_S = 2^74 and DEV = 2^70 target compressions are charged in full inside the time as upper bounds on the characteristic search behind P8, its Step-1 solve and all development (51613d1c Section 11, H4a/H4b/H4c, with the published run logs: the author's total under 2^21 core-seconds = 2^43.61 compressions, 34 bits under A_C); this submission's own development (the simulator grid, the kernel generator, 2 tuning windows, the 24 windows: under 40 core-hours, under 2^50 operations) is inside DEV. preprocessing_log2 = log2(2^78 + 2^74 + 2^70) = 78.09276.
heuristics.scope: The P8 characteristic as published and used here as data; this program's development.
heuristics.extrapolation: None: the allowances are charged, not estimated.
heuristics.limitations: The allowances are 51613d1c's upper bounds on another author's search; they are 0.0422% of this time bound.

heuristics.statement: Prices of proof.md Section 4 (collision-frontier-v5, C = 2728): one operation per 256-bit word primitive, 2 per compare-and-branch, 3 per load or store, one operation per executed kernel record (a 2-input gate on 256-bit registers, stored in 5 bytes; the price of 6b678689, 0c1ef7c3, d90878ff, 19034ce3 and 0b2616e3), one target compression = 2728; the generator of the two kernel images is charged at the cap 2^21 operations per window; the program's own control flow is charged by explicit allowances (16 per DP hit, 4 per iteration, 1024 per stage-2 phase, above the counted decisions of the handlers); every other operation passes through the counter Mach (m.o).
heuristics.scope: experiments/r38joint.py as shipped; the kernel images (1195-1270 records, at most 159 registers) are verified against the scalar maps on 256 lanes in r38-p8-claw trial 0 and selftest.
heuristics.extrapolation: None: prices, not estimates. The generator's own builder-call census is at most 2,880 calls per window, a factor over 728 under the charged cap.
heuristics.limitations: The generator charge is a declared cap, not an executed-operator count (0.3% of the work).

heuristics.statement: The peak memory is at most the declared 1,100,000 bytes = 2^20.0691: the allocation inventory of proof.md Section 6, every allocation of the attack path charged at its ALLOCATED size, enumerates 1,045,840 bytes (register file s.R=[0]*512: 16,384; lane array 8,192; save area 1,024; table 884,736; queue 32,800; stage-2 stack, pair maps and wheel 16,384; two kernel images at the cap 13,000; the shipped program text 42,600 bytes charged in full as code; per-window scalars 8,192; live temporaries of the deepest call chain 8,192; local register copies of the simulator during a kernel call 7,680; the one retained collision pair 1,024; held constants 1,536; module-level derived data 4,096), and the remaining 54,160 bytes are a declared margin for temporaries the enumeration may not name (interpreter frames, integer and string boxing, measurement-off containers): the declared figure is an upper bound, not the exact peak. The peak is bounded over the control flow: every growable container has a code-enforced cap or an allocation bound (generator gate list GEN_MAX, queue QCAP with a hard halt, stage-2 pairs NSLOT, exactly one retained collision pair since every loop exits on success, Mach dicts keyed by literal names), the attack loop releases a window before building the next, the generator's scratch exists before the table is allocated, and the measurement containers are created only when measure=True (never in --attack).
heuristics.scope: experiments/r38joint.py as shipped, setup and run (one peak; no solver, no precomputation).
heuristics.limitations: The code charge is the literal byte length of the shipped program, above any 36-byte-per-instruction encoding of the executed instructions (block census 7,213 operations); the organizer verifier does not measure memory. The predecessor eab3eea4 charged 256 register words for the 512 allocated and was refuted for it; this inventory charges the allocation.

restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words. Output: two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1' with a common first block M0 (the padding block that follows is identical); the program recomputes both complete 3-block digests before it outputs anything.

Algorithm (proof.md Section 3; experiments/r38joint.py): per first block one window of 2^25 evaluations of the 256-lane bit-sliced walk step on 29-bit points (A side: a0 in window R = 9 with one of the window's four heads; B side: u), distinguished points with six zero low bits, a bucketed table of 27,648 words x 6 entries of 40 bits with keep-longer replacement, stage-2 catch-up in 128 lane pairs, exact offset test on every cross-side collision, post-filters C1 C2 G F7 on the real words, step 3b as two charged 38-step compressions.

Cost: total charged work at most W_BUDGET + R + 6 B operations over at most B = 3227292921399400871242 windows (proof.md Section 7), plus the allowances 2^78 + 2^74 + 2^70 compressions: time_log2 = 89.3032 (exact 89.30319). Memory at most 1,100,000 bytes (enumerated 1,045,840 plus a declared margin); score 89.3723 = 89.3032 + (20.0691 - 20). Success probability at least 0.39 - exp(-2^6.7) - exp(-2^12.7) > 0.39 under H1-walk-model, H1-P1-postfilter-law and H2-P1-q3-transfer.

Probability space: fresh independent algorithmic coins for the first blocks (os.urandom in --attack); the measurements and experiments use seeds only for reproducibility. The success event is a verified collision of the complete target.

The 24 evaluation windows were pre-declared (seeds, adoption rule, program hash) before the first run and all 24 are used; organizer experiments r38-p8-claw and r38-window-small are hard-asserted in the program.
